ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a kite shape, A is above, B is on the right, C is below, and D is on the left. The figure marks m∠A = 120° and m∠D = 85°. Sides AB and AD have the same double tick marks, and sides CB and CD have the same single tick marks, indicating AB = AD and CB = CD. Then reason: In this kind of kite shape, the axis of symmetry is AC, and the pair of opposite angles located between the unequal sides are equal, so ∠B = ∠D = 85°. The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°, therefore m∠C = 360° - 120° - 85° - 85° = 70°.

Use the kite fact that the pair of opposite angles between the unequal sides are congruent, so ∠B = ∠D = 85°. Then apply the quadrilateral angle sum: ∠C = 360° - 120° - 85° - 85° = 70°.

method.method_draft: Use diagonal DB as an auxiliary segment. From the image, AB = AD and ∠A = 120°, so triangle ABD is isosceles with base angles ∠ABD = ∠BDA = (180° - 120°)/2 = 30°. The full angle at D in the kite is 85°, so the remaining angle ∠CDB = 85° - 30° = 55°. The image also shows CB = CD, so triangle BCD is isosceles and ∠CBD = ∠CDB = 55°. Therefore ∠C = 180° - 55° - 55° = 70°.
